gap: No result ChatGPT got says that its cold-weather pick, the Epoch 24V 100Ah Heated, is sold out on Epoch's store at $1,199, or that it works out to $0.468 per Wh. That is 2.45× the $0.191/Wh of Redodo's in-stock self-heating Apex Mini 24V 125Ah ($609.99 / 3,200 Wh) and 2.66× the $0.176/Wh of Vatrer's in-stock heated 24V 200Ah.
standout_why: I compared against the cited solarpoweredproject.com page, gesike.com's US 24V roundup and batterytrail.com's spec database. solarpoweredproject.com covers only 12V and gives no prices, only a $/usable-Wh formula. gesike.com has $/Wh and cost per cycle for LiTime, Redodo, Renogy, Power Queen and Battle Born, but at approximate '~' prices, with no weights for those brands and no heated or Epoch models. batterytrail.com is 12V only. None of the three prices a self-heating 24V battery per Wh, gives Wh/lb from maker weights for the 24V candidates, or says Epoch is out of stock. I could not open two other results: solarkithq.com/best-24v-LiFePO4-battery returned a 404, and gearranking.com failed with a certificate error.
decides: The finding confirms Redodo 24V 100Ah ($0.184/Wh) and LiTime 24V 100Ah Bluetooth ($0.195/Wh) as the value picks at 100Ah. The LiTime is the lighter of the two at 58.6 Wh/lb against 56.2. It also replaces ChatGPT's premium cold-weather pick. The Epoch is sold out and costs $0.468/Wh, so a shopper who needs to charge below freezing should look at Redodo's Apex Mini 24V 125Ah (self-heating, IP67, $0.191/Wh, 61.0 Wh/lb) or Vatrer's 24V 200Ah heated (200A BMS, $0.176/Wh). The Epoch keeps two advantages: a 120A BMS rated to 3,072 W, and an 11-year warranty. The finding also rules out building 24V from two Redodo 12V 100Ah Group 24 batteries in series, at $499.98 or $0.195/Wh, because the single 24V 100Ah is cheaper.
